purpose: Reliability-hardening autofix for audit issue #300 (api-data-fetching): reconstructs review-comment threads via a shared single-pass gatherReviewThread helper with by-id ancestor fallback and cycle guards, adds a bounded ascending window plus by-id fallback for issue-comment @mention context, tracks failed file batches and discloses them with a 'Partial review' banner, keys the lessons cache by the file set, makes audit dedup fail-open with a per-process registry, maps GitHub-style sort direction in the GitLab adapter, threads AbortSignal through the API layer, and gates the opencode release-lookup token to GitHub Actions with an anonymous fallback.
riskRationale: No critical or security defects: typecheck, Biome lint, and the full suite (782 lib + 20 app + 16 action tests) pass, and every previously-reported critical/important finding (ambient-token leakage to api.github.com, issue-comment ordering vs the ascending-only endpoint, dead signal plumbing, duplicated chain-walk logic, O(n-squared) walks, missing cycle guards) is fixed and covered by regression tests. Risk is medium rather than low because two important robustness gaps remain: the issue-comment by-id fallback still answers @mentions on PRs with more than 500 comments using zero preceding context, and gatherReviewThread swallows window-fetch failures that the reply flow misreports as 'Comment not found'. The audit dedup registry is also per-process and cannot bound cross-run duplicates.
breakingChanges: PlatformAdapter interface requires the new getIssueComment() method - external implementers must add it; paginate()/getReviewCommentThread()/getIssueComments() signature extensions (options/signal) are optional and backward compatible

text: A well-structured, well-tested resilience pass that resolves nearly all previously-reported critical and important findings: the shared gatherReviewThread helper eliminates the duplicated chain-walk logic with cycle guards, O(1) by-id indexing, and partial-chain resilience; the issue-comment gatherer now honors GitHub's ascending-only contract with a by-id trigger fallback; failedBatches surfaces as a 'Partial review' banner; the lessons cache is keyed by the file set; audit dedup fails open; AbortSignal is genuinely wired through the API layer; and the opencode release token is gated to GitHub Actions. What remains are bounded-window context tradeoffs on busy PRs and a few narrow error-handling and wiring gaps, all small and localized.

reasoning: Two important issues remain: on PRs with more than 500 issue comments the by-id fallback answers the @mention with only the trigger comment, losing all preceding conversation context on exactly the busy PRs this change targets; and gatherReviewThread swallows window-fetch failures that the reply flow misreports as 'Comment not found' (and any future throwOnError usage would turn a fetch blip into a false not-found). Both fixes are small, localized, and low-risk, so an automated agent can address them safely.

message: Extracting the in_reply_to_id chain walk into a shared gatherReviewThread helper is the right architectural move: it eliminates the near-duplicate, previously-divergent implementations in GitHubHelper.getReviewCommentThread and conversation.ts, indexes the window in a Map for O(1) lookups, guards cyclic/malformed chains with visited sets, resolves in-window ancestors from the map without re-fetching, direct-fetches only genuinely missing ancestors, and returns a partial chain instead of dropping the whole thread when a single fetch fails. Regression tests cover the duplicate-ID and cyclic-chain cases.

failedBatches is propagated into the final ReviewResult through the batch loop, the synthesis-fallback branch, and the linter-dedup rebuild (verified by a regression test), and review-body.ts renders it as a prominent 'Partial review' banner so consumers and the autofix loop can reliably tell findings may be incomplete. Keying the lessons cache by the sorted, deduplicated file-path set is also a correct bug fix that stops lessons from one file set silently leaking to another within the TTL.

The token-handling rework fixes the credential-leak finding properly: the ambient GITHUB_TOKEN/INPUT_GITHUB_TOKEN is only attached when GITHUB_ACTIONS === 'true' (so a GitLab CI token or local credential is never sent to api.github.com), 401/403/404 degrade to an anonymous retry, 403 was removed from the retryable set so a deterministic repo-scoped-token rejection fails fast instead of burning backoff, and a non-array assets body now yields a clear 'Release not found' error instead of a confusing TypeError.

The AbortSignal wiring correctly closes the already-aborted race: api()/graphql() check signal.aborted before registering the abort listener, abort the per-attempt controller, and clean up via removeEventListener in finally, so a signal that aborts between withRetry's top-of-loop check and listener registration can no longer leave an attempt uncancellable. The signal is genuinely plumbed from the conversation handler down to api()/paginate()/graphql(), with the identical guard in the GitLab adapter and a dedicated test asserting an already-aborted fetch is issued cancelled.

The fail-open audit dedup path is well balanced: a failed existing-issue search warns and still creates the issue (findings are never silently dropped), the per-process lastAuditIssueByCategory registry bounds duplicate accumulation within a single process, and core.setFailed is reserved for the genuine case where the issue write itself fails. The integration suite covers update-instead-of-duplicate, fail-open create, and reuse-on-repeated-outage.

On PRs with more than 500 issue comments the @mention trigger falls outside the ascending 5-page window (GitHub's GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{number}/comments ignores sort/direction and always returns oldest-first), so the triggerIdx === -1 branch direct-fetches only the trigger and sets contextComments = [triggerComment]. The model therefore receives zero preceding conversation turns on exactly the busy PRs the window-size bump was meant to serve, silently degrading to a context-free reply and undermining the PR's stated goal of reliably preserving conversation context.
suggestion: Fetch the tail of the conversation instead of the head: use the GraphQL repository.pullRequest.issueComments(last: N) connection, or extend getIssueComment to return created_at and re-fetch with a `since` parameter set to the trigger's created_at, then take the 5 comments preceding the trigger. Keep the by-id path only for genuinely old triggers.

message: gatherReviewThread catches any listReviewComments failure and returns { chain: [], comments: [] }, erasing the distinction between a transient window-fetch failure and a genuinely missing comment. Both callers then misbehave: getReviewCommentThread (github.ts:968-969) throws a misleading 'Comment X not found - cannot build thread' that makes the reply webhook post a failure reply even though the comment exists, and the conversation flow silently skips the user's @mention. This is only defensive today because both adapters' paginate() is fail-open and never throws on page failures, but any future throwOnError usage or adapter change would make the failure invisible and indistinguishable from a deleted comment - precisely the class of failure this PR is hardening against.
suggestion: On a list-fetch error, fall through to the by-id chain walk (rawComments = []) instead of returning empty; the existing missingId direct-walk then fetches the trigger and its ancestors by ID, so a fetch failure degrades to N+1 fetches rather than a false 'not found'. If the by-id walk also fails, the partial-chain logic still yields an empty result without masking the cause.

message: The AbortSignal plumbing added throughout the API layer is never exercised by the reply flow: handleReply has no signal parameter and app/src/subscribers/reply.ts:16-40 discards its signal, so a cancelled reply webhook cannot abort the up-to-10-page window fetch or the sequential by-id chain walk. This leaves the cancellation guarantees inconsistent with the @mention flow (conversation.ts), which does forward the signal.
suggestion: Thread the subscriber's AbortSignal through handleReply (add a signal?: AbortSignal parameter) and forward it to gh.getReviewCommentThread(parentCommentId, prNumber, signal) so the reply flow's windowed list and by-id fallback are cancellable like the conversation flow.

message: The lastAuditIssueByCategory dedup registry is per-process, but each GitHub Action workflow run is a fresh process with an empty registry. During a persistent search outage every run therefore falls through to the create branch and posts a brand-new duplicate audit issue - the unbounded accumulation this change set out to bound. The integration test only proves intra-process reuse by calling runAudit twice in one process, which never happens in production, so the primary fail-open duplicate-bounding goal is not fully met.
suggestion: Persist the last created/updated issue number durably across runs (e.g., embed it in the audit-update marker body or store it in a repo-level state file/issue) so a subsequent fail-open run can update the previous issue instead of creating a new one, or narrow the code comment to state the mitigation applies only within a single process invocation.

message: The 'degrades to an anonymous lookup when the authenticated release request returns 403' test sets GITHUB_TOKEN but never sets GITHUB_ACTIONS='true' (nor restores it). Since ambientToken is only attached when GITHUB_ACTIONS === 'true', the assertion that the first fetch carries 'Authorization: Bearer some-token' only holds because the ambient CI runner exports GITHUB_ACTIONS=true; run locally or in non-Actions CI the first request is anonymous and the test fails. The test's pass/fail is environment-dependent, not deterministic.
suggestion: Set process.env.GITHUB_ACTIONS = 'true' alongside GITHUB_TOKEN at the start of the test and restore both in a finally block, so the authenticated path is exercised deterministically regardless of the host environment.

message: Two edge cases in the anonymous release fallback: (1) removing 403 from retryableStatuses conflates genuine auth rejections with unauthenticated rate-limit 403s (X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0), so an anonymous rate-limit during setup now fails fast instead of retrying with backoff; (2) the anonymous fallback call sits outside the try/catch, so if that request itself fails the setup aborts with a raw 'HTTP 403/429: ...' message instead of a friendly error. The authenticated branch also cannot distinguish a 'tag does not exist' 404 from an auth failure, so a nonexistent version still burns the authenticated attempts first.
suggestion: For the anonymous call, distinguish rate-limit 403s (retryable with backoff when X-RateLimit-Remaining === 0) from auth 403s, wrap the anonymous fallback so its failure yields a clear 'Could not reach GitHub releases API anonymously: ...' message, and keep the existing assets guard so a 404 tag-not-found case throws a descriptive error rather than a raw TypeError.

message: The reply flow now funnels every reply event through gatherReviewThread with perPage 100 / maxPages 10, fetching up to 1000 review comments and expanding the full thread subtree, yet getReviewCommentThread consumes only result.chain (the ancestors) - the subtree is fetched and expanded but discarded. On repos with many review comments this is a real per-event API-cost and CPU regression versus the old direct chain walk, and the 10-page bound also exceeds the conversation flow's 5-page bound for the same logical operation, so the two callers of the shared helper still diverge in window budget.
suggestion: Pass a smaller window from getReviewCommentThread (e.g., { perPage: 100, maxPages: 2-3 }) and rely on the existing by-id fallback for deeper threads, or add a chain-only option to gatherReviewThread that skips the subtree BFS; align the window bound with the conversation flow.

message: The subtree BFS uses Array.prototype.shift() inside the loop, which is O(n) per element due to re-indexing, making the expansion O(n-squared) worst case for a window of up to 1000 comments - contradicting the docstring's 'single-pass O(n)' claim. The same quadratic pattern recurs in getReviewCommentThread where chainIds dedup uses chainIds.includes(c.id).
suggestion: Replace queue.shift() with a head-indexed loop (let head = 0; while (head < queue.length) { const parentId = queue[head++] as number; ... }) to keep the BFS linear, and use a Set for chainIds dedup.

message: The filePath expression chain.find((c) => c.path)?.path ?? chain[chain.length - 1]?.path is confusing and its right-hand fallback is dead: if no chain comment carries a path, the leaf (last chain entry) has no path either, so the fallback never adds anything. It also silently contradicts the 'anchor on the root' comment (find() searches root-first for any ancestor with a path) and diverges from the reply flow's root-anchored semantics in github.ts:962-963.
suggestion: Simplify to a single documented rule - prefer the root, then fall back to the first chain comment with a path - and drop the dead `?? chain[chain.length - 1]?.path` term so both flows anchor identically.

message: When a mid-chain by-id fetch fails, the missing-walk breaks and returns a PARTIAL chain whose first element is not the true thread root. GitHubHelper.getReviewCommentThread exposes chain[0] as rootComment and handleReply gates on rootComment.isBot (reply.ts:37), so a truncated chain can present a mid-thread user comment as the 'root' and silently skip replying to a bot-originated thread - trading the old visible failure for a silent one.
suggestion: Have gatherReviewThread signal truncation (e.g., a truncated: true flag or the leaf/trigger id) and, when the chain is incomplete, base the reply-flow isBot gate and prompt root on the guaranteed-present trigger comment (parentCommentId) so replies are not silently dropped.

message: The subtree BFS (childrenByParent) only scans the bounded window, so sibling and nested replies that fall outside the window are silently omitted from the reconstructed thread. For a deep/old thread whose trigger was recovered by by-id fetch, the older sibling replies are still missing - the exact 'never drop prior turns' intent the helper documents. The limitation is now documented but unhandled, and it persists from the previously-reported conversation flow finding.
suggestion: At minimum log a warning when the direct-fetch fallback recovers an out-of-window comment whose sibling replies are known to be absent, so operators can tell the reconstructed thread is incomplete; a full fix requires a targeted follow-up fetch (e.g., GET /pulls/{n}/comments?since=) seeded from the recovered ancestors.
